newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent firm on ACCESS, weather seen support.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent firm on ACCESS, weather seen support.

text.p: Brent February crude futures in Asia were firmer in late trading on Monday maintaining an arbitrage around $1.47 with front-month NYMEX crude.
February Brent last traded at $24.25 per barrel, up 13 cents from the London settlement on Friday.
Brokers said there was a pocket of resistance around $24.30 but they expected the cold Arctic snap in Europe and forecasts for below average temperatures in the northeast U.S. to support the market.
"On the back of the weather, I don't see any reason to sell this market," one broker said.
NYMEX crude February was last traded at $25.77, up 18 cents from New York on Friday where prices had fallen 10 cents on the back of a weak heating oil contract.
The contract fell briefly below support at $25.50 in New York but then rebounded. The rebound was extended on ACCESS.

February heating oil retraced its Friday losses on ACCESS Monday but by late afternoon in Asia had cooled slightly to stand at 72.00 cents per gallon -- off the intraday high of 72.10 cents -- after giving up 82 cents in New York.
